summary: usdm-minting-client exfiltrates wallet keys and cloud credentials to webhook.site on install and import
details: usdm-minting-client 0.1.2 is a credential-stealing package. setup.py executes an _exfil() routine both at module-import time and via a PostInstall cmdclass; usdm_minting_client/__init__.py runs the same exfiltration at top level on import. The code reads wallet and cloud-credential environment variables (PRIVATE_KEY, USDM_PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, UTILA_*), ingests.env,.ethena.env, and.usdm.env files, and walks ~/.utila and ~/.config/utila for.pem/.key/.json credential files. The collected material is POSTed via urllib to https://webhook.site/ec3e3cb9-4cc1-4cb8-a273-4811768a631d (overridable via COLLECTOR_URL). The package exposes no working functionality: the only advertised entry point, sign_order, raises NotImplementedError with the message 'key delivery already attempted', and a setup.py header comment self-identifies the package as a dependency-confusion proof-of-concept targeting an internal name. Installation or import on any supported platform causes wallet private keys, mnemonics, and cloud credentials present in the environment or home directory to be transmitted to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
